subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If x² − 6x + 5 = 0 and x² − 12x + p = 0 have a common root, then find p.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this — say which equation you solve first and why, and what you do with each root you get.
insider_note: The first equation has no unknown, so solve it and take both roots forward — each one gives its own p. Subtracting the equations instead mixes p and x in one line and solves nothing.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the common root
steps.margin_note: First mark. One of the two equations has no unknown in it — solve THAT one. x² − 6x + 5 = (x − 1)(x − 5), so the common root can only be 1 or 5.
steps.memory_tip: The first equation has no unknown, so it fixes α: (x − 1)(x − 5) = 0 gives 1 or 5.
lines: Let α be the common root.

recall.must_convey: That the common root α must satisfy the fully known equation x² − 6x + 5 = 0, which factorises as (α − 1)(α − 5) = 0, so α = 1 or 5.
accept: the common root satisfies x squared minus six x plus five equals zero which factorises to give one or five
solve the first equation because it has no unknown, the roots are one and five
let alpha be the common root, from the first equation alpha is one or five
first equation lo unknown ledu kabatti daanini solve cheste alpha one leda five
the possible common roots are one and five
heard_as: x squared minus six x plus five

steps.why: A common root is a root of both equations; the first equation is completely known, so it fixes the common root as one of two numbers before p is touched at all.
common_mistakes: Trying to subtract the equations and getting an expression with both p and x in it.
Keeping only α = 1 and forgetting α = 5.

steps.label: Substitute in the second
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Each candidate goes into x² − 12x + p = 0. α = 1: 1 − 12 + p = 0 gives p = 11. α = 5: 25 − 60 + p = 0 gives p = 35. Two values of α, two values of p — give both.
steps.memory_tip: α = 1 gives p = 11 and α = 5 gives p = 35. Carry both candidates through.

recall.must_convey: That each candidate root is substituted into x² − 12x + p = 0, giving p = 11 for α = 1 and p = 35 for α = 5, and both values are reported.
accept: put alpha equals one into the second equation to get p eleven and alpha equals five to get p thirty five
substitute each root into x squared minus twelve x plus p equals zero, p is eleven or thirty five
one gives one minus twelve plus p zero so p eleven, five gives twenty five minus sixty plus p zero so p thirty five
alpha one pettithe p eleven, alpha five pettithe p thirty five
p equals eleven or thirty five

steps.why: The common root must also make the second equation true, and substituting is the only way p enters. Each candidate for α gives its own p, and nothing in the question rules either out.
common_mistakes: Substituting α = 1 and α = 5 into the first equation again, which gives nothing.
